title: Portfolio: visual world
question: The roll assigned the Teletext Index Service. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Teletext Index Service
options.lineage: 1980s broadcast teletext magazines (Ceefax, ITV index pages)
options.thesis: The portfolio as a text service with numbered pages: an index you scan, not a site you scroll.
options.viewport: P100 index page: name and role in mosaic type, four numbered rows with their page numbers, key row at the bottom.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty if the 40x24 grid is not strictly honoured on mobile.

raised.raise: Every project resolves like a print developing: staged and irreversible, never a fade-out.
Colour is signal only: the key row and the page numbers, never decoration.
Type is matter: the name is set as a mosaic word, not inside a logo box.
The index inks in print order, row by row, like blocks pulled one at a time.
The character grid is the only geometry, and the whole service is keyboard operable.
Every rule is drawn, never implied: hairlines at one device pixel, states as printed marks.

options.label: Green Phosphor VT100
options.lineage: DEC VT220 and Unix TTY sessions
options.thesis: The portfolio as a live shell session: you read the output and the command is the call to action.
options.viewport: Black ground, a green prompt, a short listing of projects and the contact line at the bottom.
options.risk: The direction most runs in this category land on: the most legible, and the least surprising.

options.label: ANSI Bulletin Board
options.lineage: 2 a.m. dial-up bulletin boards, CP437 title screens
options.thesis: The portfolio as a board: numbered areas, block-character chrome, one caller online.
options.viewport: Double-line frame, a block-art title, numbered areas and a presence line.
options.case: Holds the peers axis: it is the most convincing world for developers, and it loses the recruiter axis, where a board of threads hides the work.
options.risk: A board of threads is a poor shape for a body of work; the framing over the artefact.

options.label: Reference Setting
options.lineage: wide-margin reference editions, ruled by a setting engine
options.thesis: The portfolio as a printed reference work: a keyed rail down the centre, everything annotated in the margin.
options.viewport: Two columns of small roman type around a vermilion key rail, notes in a wide margin.
options.case: Holds the recruiter axis: the most legible and credible shape for a body of work. Loses the brief axis, its material is paper, not a machine.
options.risk: Reads as a different category entirely: a reference book, not a terminal.

canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
